sections.label: Reviewing drug laws and policies
sections.summary: Laws and policies are continually reviewed, with a legislative framework for psychoactive substances and a tiered punishment framework for drug possession to be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To this end, we continually review and refine our laws and policies to keep pace with the evolving drug landscape and local trends.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will be introducing a legislative framework to deal with psychoactive substances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will also be introducing a tiered punishment framework for the drug possession offence.

sections.label: NPS proliferation and abuser arrests
sections.summary: NPS detected worldwide rose from 166 in 2009 to 1,150 in 2022, and local NPS abusers arrested rose from about three yearly to about 235 yearly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Around the world, NPS are proliferating at an unprecedented rate, from just 166 NPS detected in 2009 to 1,150 in 2022, a sevenfold increase in slightly over a decade.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Locally, the number of NPS abusers arrested increased from an average of three abusers per year between 2014 and 2017, to an average of 235 per year from 2018 to 2022.

sections.label: Excluded Substances Fifth Schedule
sections.summary: A new Fifth Schedule of Excluded Substances is created so substances already regulated or with legitimate uses are not treated as psychoactive substances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The first limb of the definition of psychoactive substance is broad and may cover substances that are already regulated under other legislation or those with legitimate uses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, we have created a new Fifth Schedule of "Excluded Substances", which will not be considered as nor regulated as psychoactive substances, as reflected under the second limb of the definition of psychoactive substance.

sections.label: Punishment framework for psychoactive substances
sections.summary: The punishment framework for new psychoactive substance offences takes reference from Class C controlled drugs, generally with fines instead of caning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The punishment framework for these new offences relating to psychoactive substances will take reference from that for Class C controlled drugs, but, generally, with fines, in place of caning.

sections.label: Listing substances as controlled drugs
sections.summary: Once a substance's molecular structure is identified and industry consultation finds no legitimate use, it will be listed in the First Schedule as a controlled drug.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Once the molecular structure of a specific psychoactive substance is identified and industry consultation has been conducted to determine that the substance has no legitimate use, we will list the substance in the First Schedule as a controlled drug.

sections.label: Proving a psychoactive substance
sections.summary: Clause 15 introduces section 22A, providing that proving a substance has the capacity to have a psychoactive effect if consumed is sufficient for prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Clause 15 introduces a new section 22A, which provides that for the purpose of proving that the substance in question is a psychoactive substance, it is sufficient for the prosecution to prove that the substance has the capacity to have a psychoactive effect on an individual if consumed.

sections.label: Increased drug possession penalties
sections.summary: MHA proposes higher punishments, including caning, for possessing selected controlled drugs above certain weight thresholds, via Clause 34.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: MHA, therefore, proposes to increase punishments, which will include caning, for the possession of selected controlled drugs above certain weight thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Clause 34 amends the Second Schedule to increase the penalties for the offence of the unauthorised possession of certain quantities of selected drugs.

sections.label: Middle and highest tier sentences
sections.summary: Middle tier carries 10 to 20 years' imprisonment and five to 10 strokes of the cane; highest tier 20 to 30 years and 10 to 15 strokes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the middle tier, the minimum mandatory sentence will be 10 years' imprisonment and five strokes of the cane, while the maximum is set at 20 years' imprisonment and 10 strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the highest tier, the minimum mandatory sentence will be 20 years' imprisonment and 10 strokes of the cane, while the maximum is set at 30 years' imprisonment and 15 strokes of the cane.

sections.label: CNB investigations and prosecution process
sections.summary: CNB investigates large-quantity possession cases and recommends charges to AGC; the amendments only affect the eventual sentence after conviction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For persons in possession of large quantities of drugs, CNB will continue to conduct thorough investigations to determine if the drugs were meant for trafficking, their own consumption or otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Depending on the facts of the case, CNB will make its recommendations to the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) on the appropriate charges, for example, whether for trafficking or simply possession.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The amendments to the punishment framework do not affect this investigation and prosecution process and will only affect the eventual sentence faced by a person who is convicted of a possession offence.

sections.label: SAF Act consumption convictions clarified
sections.summary: Clause 25 amends section 33 of the MDA so only previous SAF Act drug consumption convictions, not possession, count towards enhanced punishment.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Clause 25 amends section 33 of the MDA to clarify that only previous convictions for drug consumption under section 34 of the SAF Act and not for drug possession, will count towards enhanced punishment for drug consumption under the MDA.

sections.label: CNB supervision regime regulations
sections.summary: The amendment enables regulations giving CNB case-by-case discretion if CNB and MINDEF assess the individual would benefit from CNB's supervision regime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nonetheless, this amendment will enable the making of regulations to provide CNB with the discretion to do so on a case-by-case basis, if both CNB and MINDEF assess that the individual would benefit from undergoing CNB's supervision regime in addition to MINDEF's.

sections.label: New NPS legislative framework
sections.summary: A new legislative framework is proposed to deal with NPS based on their capacity to produce a psychoactive effect rather than molecular structure.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Indeed, drug suppliers are known to tailor the molecular structure of NPS according to what is not yet controlled through legislation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Hence, we are proposing a new legislative framework to deal with the NPS threat based on their capacity to produce a psychoactive effect, rather than their molecular structure.

sections.label: Drugs under new punishment framework
sections.summary: The new punishment framework will apply to morphine, diamorphine, opium, cocaine, cannabis, cannabis resin, cannabis mixture and methamphetamine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The new punishment framework will apply to: morphine, diamorphine, opium, cocaine, cannabis, cannabis resin, cannabis mixture and methamphetamine.

sections.label: Contingencies Funds combined balance
sections.summary: There is currently a combined balance of $16 billion in the Contingencies Funds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Currently, there is a combined balance of $16 billion in the Contingencies Funds.

sections.label: Clause 4 amends Article 148C
sections.summary: Clause 4 amends Article 148C to let the Finance Minister reduce a Contingencies Fund balance if a withdrawal is in excess of what is likely necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends Article 148C to permit the Finance Minister to reduce the balance of a Contingencies Fund, if he is satisfied, after proper inquiry, that the sum to be withdrawn from the Fund is in excess of what is likely necessary to meet an urgent and unforeseen need for expenditure.

sections.label: Reducing Contingencies Funds balance
sections.summary: The Bill provides a mechanism to reduce the Contingencies Funds balance, and MOF intends to reduce it from $16 billion to $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As we return to normalcy following the COVID-19 pandemic, it is timely and prudent to reduce the Contingencies Funds balance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The amendments proposed in this Bill will provide the mechanism for us to do so and ensure greater fiscal discipline while preserving the nimbleness to deal with urgent and unforeseen needs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: After the Bill is passed, MOF intends to reduce the Contingencies Funds balance from $16 billion to $6 billion and will submit a report to Parliament when that transfer has been made.

sections.label: NPS abusers arrested in Singapore
sections.summary: NPS abusers arrested in Singapore rose from an average of three per year in 2014 to 2017 to 235 per year in 2018 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to the UNODC Commission on Narcotic Drugs, " he largest number of   are spread across three regions: Asia, Europe and North America." In Singapore, there has been an increase in the number of NPS abusers arrested, from an average of three per year in the 2014 to 2017 period to 235 per year in the 2018 to 2022 period.

sections.label: Regulating NPS by psychoactive effect
sections.summary: The proposed framework will regulate substances based on their capacity to produce a psychoactive effect rather than their chemical structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We, thus, need our legislation to be flexible enough to adapt to NPS in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the proposed framework which will regulate such substances based on their capacity to produce a psychoactive effect rather than its chemical structure.

sections.label: Safeguards for landlords and shelters
sections.summary: Asks what safeguards protect innocent landlords or shelter organisations from prosecution under two presumptions of knowledge based on presumption of possession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These are two separate presumptions of knowledge based on an initial presumption of possession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, may I ask what are the safeguards in place to protect innocent landlords or organisations running shelters from being prosecuted under these presumptions of these sections?

sections.label: Welcome for increased drug punishments
sections.summary: Welcomes the Bill's proposed increased punishments, including caning, for possessing selected controlled drugs above certain weight thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, I welcome this Bill's proposed increased punishments, including caning, for the possession of selected controlled drugs above certain weight thresholds.

sections.label: Offence of exposing child to substances
sections.summary: New section 11N makes it an offence to expose a child to any psychoactive substance or paraphernalia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The new section 11N sends such a signal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It makes it an offence for exposing a child to any psychoactive substance or paraphernalia.

sections.label: Offence of causing youth substance offences
sections.summary: Notes youth cannabis abusers below 20 caught rose threefold since 2021, and new section 11Q makes it an offence to cause or procure a young person to commit psychoactive substance offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The number of youth abusers below 20 years old caught abusing cannabis, has also increased threefold since 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill makes it a specific offence for anyone causing or procuring a young person to commit any offence relating to psychoactive substances, under the new section 11Q.

sections.label: Strategy against vaping
sections.summary: Asks the Minister of State to share MHA's strategy and actions with HSA or other agencies against vaping, which can be small and discrete and hard to detect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some are even small and discrete, making it difficult to detect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, can the Minister of State please share the strategy and actions that MHA will be taking in concert with the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) or other agencies against vaping?

sections.label: Workers' Party support for NPS regulation
sections.summary: In view of evidence of harms caused by NPS, the Workers' Party supports the rationale for regulating NPS in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of the evidence of the harms caused by NPS, the Workers' Party supports the rationale for regulating NPS in Singapore.

sections.label: Punishments for controlled drug possession
sections.summary: The Bill increases punishments for unauthorised possession of larger quantities of eight named controlled drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Next, I move to the second thrust of the Bill, to increase the punishments for unauthorised possession of larger quantities of certain controlled drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are eight drugs in question: cannabis, cannabis mixture, cannabis resin, cocaine, diamorphine, methamphetamine, morphine and opium.

sections.label: Drug weight tier cut-offs
sections.summary: The middle tier cut-off weight is 10 to 15 grammes and the upper tier is more than 15 grammes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for middle tier, the cut-off weight is set at between 10 to 15 grammes, while the upper tier is set at more than 15 grammes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is worth noting that, under the current law, trafficking in more than 15 grammes attracts the death penalty.

sections.label: Contingencies Funds balance reduction
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong said the Government raised the Contingencies Funds balance to $16 billion in May 2020 and he wished to reduce it to $6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During the Budget debate this year, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong reminded the House that in May 2020, the Government had raised the Contingencies Funds balance from $3 billion to $16 billion, in anticipation of needing unforeseen and urgent cashflow due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He noted that, with the return to normalcy, he wished to reduce the balance of the Contingencies Funds from $16 billion to $6 billion.

sections.label: Contingencies Funds transfer reporting
sections.summary: Proposed sub-Article 5 lets the Minister for Finance transfer funds out, and sub-Article 6 requires a report of every transfer to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The proposed sub-Article 5 will enable the Minister for Finance to make transfers out of the Contingencies Funds, back to the Consolidated Fund and Development Fund respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As to how Parliament will be involved in this process, the proposed sub-Article 6 will require the Minister to present a report of every transfer as soon as practicable after the transfer is made.

sections.label: NPS control framework
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a framework to control NPS by psychoactive effects rather than chemical structures, with prosecution proving capacity to produce a psychoactive effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the reductions in the balances will also require a reporting to Parliament, will the Minister explain what form this reporting will take, such as what information will be provided and how Members can participate in this process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will introduce a framework to control NPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This results in new substances that have the same effect as illicit drugs, but are now not regulated under Misuse of Drugs laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill will allow us to regulate NPS in a nimble way by controlling substances based on their ability to produce psychoactive effects rather than on their chemical structures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To prove that a substance is a psychoactive substance under the new section 22A, the prosecution only has to prove that a product has the capacity to produce a psychoactive effect.

sections.label: Children in drug raids
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will work with MSF and social service agencies to ensure children in drug raids are cared for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry work with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the relevant social service agencies, before and after a drug raid, to ensure that the children in these situations are cared for appropriately?

sections.label: NPS numbers worldwide
sections.summary: NPS internationally outnumber controlled psychoactive substances almost three times, with 1,150 identified NPS across 134 countries in the 2022 UNODC report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The number of NPS internationally far exceeds the number of controlled psychoactive substances by almost three times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the 2022 report by UNODC, it was recorded that there were 1,150 identified NPS across 134 countries, with 50 new ones being recorded since the year before.

sections.label: NPS situation in Singapore
sections.summary: NPS are Singapore's third most commonly abused drug, with a sharp increase in synthetic cannabinoid seizures over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The global and regional situation is reflected in Singapore, where NPS are the third most commonly abused drug and there is a sharp increase in seizures of synthetic cannabinoids over the last five years.

sections.label: NPS appeal to younger generation
sections.summary: One in four local drug abusers is under 30, including more than 50% of new abusers, so the trend of NPS attracting the young must be monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Earlier, I mentioned the trend of NPS being particularly attractive to the younger generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I think we have to carefully monitor that, because one in four drug abusers locally is under 30 years of age and that includes more than 50% of new abusers.

sections.label: Overseas syndicates and ASEAN cooperation
sections.summary: Many syndicates and their masterminds are overseas and outside jurisdiction, so closer cooperation with bilateral counterparts and ASEAN platforms like ASOD is hoped for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is not easy as many of the syndicates are based overseas, and their masterminds are also not within our jurisdiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope that we can have even closer cooperation with our bilateral counterparts, such as the various platforms within ASEAN that deal specifically with this issue, including the Meetings of the ASEAN Senior Officials on Drug Matters (ASOD).

sections.label: Shifting regional attitudes towards drugs
sections.summary: The member asks whether Singapore can commit resources to such efforts, noting shifting regional government attitudes including more tolerance or acceptance of recreational drug use like cannabis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can Singapore play a role in committing some resources to such efforts?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There are also shifting attitudes among governments in the region towards drugs, including some showing more tolerance or even acceptance of recreational uses for selected types of drugs, like cannabis.

sections.label: Mental health support for abusers
sections.summary: Studies show substance abuse and mental health issues often co-occur, so the member requests more comprehensive, longer-term mental health resources and support for rehabilitated drug abusers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Studies have also shown that substance abuse and mental health issues are often co-occurring disorders and abusers require longer-term support, treatment and guidance in order to have a better chance at rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, can I request for more comprehensive and longer-term mental health resources and support for drug abusers who have gone through rehabilitation?

sections.label: NPS safeguards and schedule reviews
sections.summary: MP asks about safeguards for examining new NPS and the robustness and frequency of First and Fifth Schedule reviews.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given that NPSs are inherently new, can the Minister share what safeguards are in place to ensure that any newly discovered NPS is thoroughly examined before its inclusion or exclusion in the Fifth Schedule?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There have also been efforts to develop synthetic cannabinoids for medical use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, I seek the Minister's explanation on the robustness and frequency of reviews of the First and Fifth Schedules, to ensure both remain updated for our drug control approach that impedes our scientific and medical research initiatives, yet did not play catch-up with the ever-evolving drug variants.

sections.label: Saliva test kit for NPS
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to clarify whether the new saliva test kit can detect NPS consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify if the new saliva test kit can detect NPS consumption?

sections.label: Youth NPS numbers
sections.summary: MP asks for the equivalent number used by youths in relation to NPS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As a matter of record, can he also provide the equivalent number used by our youths, in relation to NPS?

sections.label: Definition of drug addict
sections.summary: Clause 2(b) amends the section 2 definition of drug addict to include psychoactive substance use causing desire, need or dependence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 2(b) amends the definition of "drug addict" in section 2 to include a person who, through the use of any psychoactive substance, has developed a desire or need to continue to take that psychoactive substance or a psychological or physical dependence upon the effect of that psychoactive substance.

sections.label: Enhanced drug rehabilitation regimes
sections.summary: In 2014 the EDRR was introduced for first- and second-time abusers; in 2019 it was enhanced for third-time and subsequent abusers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, in 2014, the enhanced drug rehabilitation regime (EDRR) was introduced for first- and second-time drug abusers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2019, the drug rehabilitation regime was further enhanced to commit third-time and subsequent drug abusers who are not charged with any other criminal offences to DRC.

sections.label: Youth substance abuse trends
sections.summary: Pandemic data suggests youths did not turn to illicit substances, but CNB director said abuse of certain substances is returning to pre-pandemic levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is positive news, as it suggests that despite the increased social stresses and anxieties brought about by the pandemic, illicit substances were not an avenue that youths turned to, to seek relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, Mr Sam Tee, the current director of CNB added in an interview in November 2021, that abuse among youths of certain substances is quickly returning to pre-pandemic levels.

sections.label: Anti-addiction campaign using TikTok
sections.summary: The "What's Your Fix?" campaign used social media apps like TikTok to teach how addictions develop and encourage positive decisions rather than scare youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Titled "What's Your Fix?", the campaign sought to develop an understanding on how addictions develop, and employed social media apps, such as TikTok, to impart knowledge and encourage positive decision-making, rather than scaring our youths.

sections.label: Youth delinquency and family disruption
sections.summary: A 2021 MSF report links adverse childhood experiences and family disruptions to earlier, heavier drug abuse, prompting a call to prioritise family cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the 2021 report on youth delinquency by MSF, youth offenders who have experienced adverse childhood experiences are more likely to engage in drug abuse at a younger age and with a greater dependency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The report also highlighted that family disruptions are a significant factor hindering the social and emotional development of children and increasing the likelihood of substance abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, I urge this House to also prioritise strategies to support family cohesion and address the underlying issues that contribute to family disruptions, especially where parents are already users, while we introduce these amendments to MDA.

sections.label: Returning Contingencies Fund money
sections.summary: Returning funds from the Contingencies Fund to the Consolidated or Development Fund needs no vote, only a Miscellaneous Paper from the Minister for Finance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The transfer of funds, from the Contingencies Funds to the Consolidated Fund or Development Fund, does not involve the appropriation of funds for Government spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As such, it does not need to be specifically voted upon when we are returning it, and therefore, informing Parliament is sufficient, given that Parliament initially authorised the top-up of the Contingencies Fund via the supply process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in specific response to the question, the form it would take would be a Miscellaneous Paper from the Minister for Finance, which would be submitted to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I do not have the exact wording with me, but it will say something like "There will be a reduction of X dollars from Contingencies Fund returned to the Consolidated Fund", and Members can then, if they wish, ask Parliamentary Questions.

sections.label: Presumptions under MDA since 1973
sections.summary: The presumptions have existed since MDA was introduced in 1973 and have worked well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The presumptions have been in existence since the introduction of MDA in 1973 and they have worked well.

sections.label: Defences for new psychoactive substances
sections.summary: The Bill gives NPS specific defences not applying to traditional controlled drugs, such as proving the substance is excluded or intended for a legitimate non-consumption purpose.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, the Bill contains specific defences for NPS that do not apply to traditional controlled drugs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, it is a valid defence for an individual to prove that the psychoactive substance is an excluded substance or that he intended to use the psychoactive substance for a legitimate purpose other than human consumption.

sections.label: Landlords renting with exclusive possession
sections.summary: Landlords who rent premises to others have nothing to fear if they have given tenants exclusive possession of the property.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Landlords who simply rent their premises to others have nothing to fear if they have given the tenants exclusive possession of the property.

sections.label: Presumption of knowledge elements
sections.summary: New section 18A(2) is one presumption of knowledge, with section 22B setting out two elements of that knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To address Mr Zhulkarnain's point about there being two separate presumptions of knowledge based on an initial presumption of possession, I should clarify that the new section 18A(2) represents only one presumption of knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I explained in my opening speech, the new section 22B provides that such knowledge comprises two elements – it is established if the person knew the substance had the capacity to have a psychoactive effect on an individual when consumed and did not know or have reason to believe that the substance is an excluded substance.

sections.label: Synthetic cannabinoid listed
sections.summary: In June 2022 a synthetic cannabinoid was listed in the First Schedule after first being detected in November 2021.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, in June 2022, we listed a synthetic cannabinoid in the First Schedule after it was first detected in circulation in November 2021.

sections.label: CNB test kits cannot detect NPS
sections.summary: The test kits presently deployed by CNB cannot detect NPS.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Presently, the test kits deployed by CNB cannot detect NPS.

sections.label: Syndicates smuggling larger drug quantities
sections.summary: CNB has observed drug syndicates smuggling larger quantities of drugs per transaction, which may drive up local demand and cause downstream law and order issues.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: CNB has observed, in recent years, that drug syndicates are smuggling larger quantities of drugs per transaction.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We are concerned that this may drive up demand locally and may cause downstream law and order issues.

sections.label: Seeking Commission on Narcotic Drugs membership
sections.summary: MHA and CNB plan to seek membership at the global Commission of Narcotic Drugs for the 2024 to 2027 term.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, MHA and CNB plan to further their commitment to the international fight against drugs by seeking membership at the global Commission of Narcotic Drugs for the 2024 to 2027 term.

sections.label: Alerting MSF when child present
sections.summary: Even if a caregiver remains for the child after the arrest, CNB will still alert MSF if the child was at the scene.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Even if there remains a caregiver for the child after the arrest, CNB will still alert MSF as long as the child was at the scene of the arrest.

sections.label: Community support for ex-drug abusers
sections.summary: MHA says ex-drug abusers need community support, and Singapore Prison Service works with community partners to give continual support after release.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: MHA recognises that ex-drug abusers need community support in order to successfully reintegrate and not relapse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Singapore Prison Service works with various community partners like the Singapore Anti-Narcotics Association, Singapore After-Care Association and religious social service agencies, to provide continual pro-social support and engagement for drug abusers after their release.

sections.label: No need for harm reduction
sections.summary: Singapore says harm reduction has limited application and there is no benefit or need for it here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Harm reduction strategies have limited application to Singapore's drug situation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Singapore is not in a state where we cannot deal with the drug situation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Therefore, there is no benefit or need for Singapore to adopt harm reduction measures.

sections.label: Arrest risk before First Schedule listing
sections.summary: An MP asks whether people risk arrest, charges or DRC referral for substances with psychoactive effect not yet listed in the MDA First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: My question for the Minister of State of Home Affairs is about the interim period when the Bill allows the enforcement agencies to proceed if a substance is found of a psychoactive effect, even though it has not been listed yet in the MDA First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: If there is a legitimate use, then it will not be listed in the First Schedule.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, my question is, will there be any risk that people are arrested, charged or even sent for DRC?

sections.label: Testing before arrest for new substances
sections.summary: With built and previously detected capabilities testing can be quick, but without confirmation of new substances no arrest will be made.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: What is key is that with the capabilities that we have built and those that we have detected before, we will be able to test quickly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: But there will be new ones where, if we have not got any confirmation, we will not arrest the person.

sections.label: Tests and consultations before action
sections.summary: The speaker assures Ms Lim that robust tests and consultations will be carried out before any action is taken.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Once we do that, we will be able to investigate further and work with the industry before we make and carry out any action.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, I want to assure Ms Lim that we will carry out a robust set of tests and consultations before we take any action.
